title: Will AI replace Software Engineers ? Raw & Honest Opinion
summary: Hindi-language personal take: AI shrinks delivery time, threatens junior roles, and developers must learn AI.

verdicts.note: Hiring data (e.g. Stanford 'canaries' 2025) shows junior roles hit harder than senior, but evidence that senior demand rose is weaker.

assertions.quote: two-week sprint work can now be done in an hour or even five minutes

verdicts.note: Some small greenfield features do go that fast, but controlled studies show modest average gains (or slowdowns) on real work; testing, review and deployment don't shrink 100x.
Across 201 enterprise developers, average throughput rose by about one user story per week (+18%), nothing like compressing multi-week sprints into hours (pre-agentic tools).

assertions.quote: they are laying off people so they can put that money into AI

verdicts.note: Several firms (Salesforce, Microsoft, Amazon) tied cuts or hiring freezes to AI investment, but cost cutting and macro factors explain much of it.

assertions.quote: we have to go through it and review it; we cannot follow everything blindly

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.
The review concludes that skill in verification, constraint specification and review may matter as much as authoring skill, and that the central risk is a verification gap.

assertions.quote: AI will surely replace the people who are not learning AI

verdicts.note: A slogan about future labor competition, not a testable claim; plausible but unmeasured.

assertions.quote: obviously AI is making us dumb

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.
The review describes 'cognitive debt': deferring understanding during fast iteration raises later debugging and maintenance costs. It does not measure skill loss directly.
